gloss: sweets; desserts (a stylish, modern-feeling word for confections, especially Western-style)

definitions.gloss: sweets; desserts; pastries (Western-style or modern Japanese-style confections)
definitions.explanation: Sweet foods, especially Western-style desserts such as cakes, tarts, parfaits, and pastries, but also stylishly presented Japanese sweets. The word entered everyday Japanese in the 2000s and now strongly implies fashionable, café-style confections suitable for posting to social media. It is more upscale and trendy in feel than お{菓子|かし}, which can mean any kind of snack or sweet.

examples.japanese: スイーツが{大好|だいす}きだ。
{駅前|えきまえ}に{新|あたら}しいスイーツのお{店|みせ}ができた。
examples.english: A new sweets shop has opened in front of the station.

examples.japanese: {季節|きせつ}{限定|げんてい}のスイーツを{食|た}べに{出|で}かけた。
examples.english: We went out to eat seasonal limited-edition sweets.

examples.japanese: コンビニのスイーツは{年々|ねんねん}クオリティーが{上|あ}がっていて、{有名|ゆうめい}{店|てん}と{遜色|そんしょく}ないものも{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Convenience-store sweets have been improving in quality year by year, and many rival those of famous shops.

notes:
スイーツ is the English plural "sweets" naturalized into Japanese as a fashionable, lifestyle-oriented word for desserts. It became popular in the 2000s, partly through TV food coverage, and now refers to a broad category of café and shop confections — especially photogenic Western-style desserts like cakes, tarts, parfaits, macarons, and pancakes.

USAGE:
- Café and dessert-shop menus
- Convenience-store premium dessert lines (コンビニスイーツ)
- Hotel afternoon-tea sets and seasonal fairs
- Social-media food posts
- スイーツ has a distinctly cosmopolitan, Instagrammable connotation. A handful of {煎餅|せんべい} would not normally be called スイーツ.
- The word can be used as a count noun in phrases like スイーツを{二|ふた}つ{選|えら}ぶ "to pick two desserts."
- For polite restaurant menus, デザート is more common than スイーツ.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- スイーツ{店|てん} / スイーツショップ: dessert shop
- {季節|きせつ}{限定|げんてい}スイーツ: seasonal limited-edition dessert
- コンビニスイーツ: convenience-store dessert
- {和|わ}スイーツ: "Japanese-style sweets" — a marketing term for Japanese confections styled as modern desserts
- スイーツ{男子|だんし}: a man who enjoys eating and shopping for sweets
- スイーツ{巡|めぐ}り: a sweets tour, going from shop to shop

SIMILAR / RELATED TERMS:
- お{菓子|かし}: sweets, snacks — the general native word, covering everything from rice crackers and chocolate bars to traditional Japanese confections. Much broader than スイーツ.
- デザート: dessert — usually a course at the end of a meal
- {洋菓子|ようがし}: Western-style confections (cakes, cookies, etc.) — a more traditional category label, somewhat overlapping with スイーツ but less trendy in feel
- {和菓子|わがし}: traditional Japanese confections (e.g., {大福|だいふく}, {羊羹|ようかん}); not normally called スイーツ except in modern marketing as "{和|わ}スイーツ"
- {甘|あま}いもの: sweet things — a casual, native expression for "sweet stuff" in general
